Article (plain text of the PDF):

Rational Linear Relations and Laplace Equations for Two-Loop
Dihedral Modular Graph Functions at Weights 3 to 9
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles

Preprint, October 4, 2026
Abstract
We study rational linear relations among two-loop dihedral modular graph functions
C(a, b, c) of weight w = 3, 5, 7, 9, the Eisenstein series E(w) and ζ(w). We also study Laplace
equations for C(2, 1, 1), C(3, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 1). Counting predictions for such relation spaces
come from generating-series methods (arXiv:2004.05156, quoted in); the explicit weight-9
relation was not found there in our search. At each weight we find a relation space of dimension
exactly 1, including the weight-9 relation −2160 C(4, 4, 1) − 4320 C(4, 3, 2) − 960 C(3, 3, 3) +
960 E(9) + ζ(9) = 0. The Laplace equations hold with sources built from Eisenstein series
and ζ(5). The method is exact leading Laurent coefficients, high-precision evaluation at
verifier-chosen points and a singular-value gap for completeness. All statements are numerical
observations, not theorems. This is a pre-release: the computation at weight eleven is still
running and the results are preliminary.
Keywords: modular graph functions, string theory, Laplace equations, non-holomorphic
Eisenstein series, zeta values, lattice sums

1

Introduction

Modular graph functions arise as coefficients of the low-energy expansion of the one-loop closedstring amplitude. The two-loop dihedral functions C(a, b, c) satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations
with inhomogeneous terms polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series (arXiv:1502.06698,
quoted in). Identities among them were proved for weight less than six (arXiv:1603.00839, quoted
in). All identities at weight six and all dihedral identities at weight seven were later obtained
and proven (arXiv:1608.04393v3, quoted in). A counting of linearly independent modular graph
forms at fixed weight, with predictions, is given in arXiv:2004.05156v2 (quoted in).
Open question: what is the complete space of rational linear relations among all C(a, b, c) of
weight w, E(w) and ζ(w) for w = 3, 5, 7, 9?
Contribution: we determine the relation space numerically at each of these weights, give
explicit relations, and test inhomogeneous Laplace equations. The weight-9 relation was not
found explicitly in our search, but it may be implied by the generating-series counting of
arXiv:2004.05156. This is a pre-release. The computation at weight eleven is still running
and all results are preliminary. Every modular-graph-function statement below is a numerical
observation.
Summary of results.
• Weight-3 observation: the relation space has dimension 1.
• Weight-5 observation: the relation space has dimension 1.
• Weight-7 observation: the relation space has dimension 1.
• Weight-9 observation: the relation space has dimension 1, with an explicit relation.
• Laplace-equation observations for C(3, 1, 1), C(2, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 1).
• Negative result: the weight-6 question, for which no claim passed the verifier.

3

Method

Trusted base: the verifier’s own evaluation of E(s) and C(a, b, c) at 32 digits at points it chooses
itself. Relations proposed by a search are not trusted; each is re-checked as follows.
1. Exact leading Laurent coefficient. For each relation reported here, the exact leading Laurent
coefficient vanishes.
2. Numerical residual. The relation is evaluated at the verifier points. The maximal relative
residual must be below 1e-24 for linear relations and below 1e-14 for Laplace equations,
where L is a finite-difference Laplacian.
3. Completeness. The normalised value matrix (rows are evaluation points, columns are the
functions) is decomposed by singular values, with evaluation seed 4712. The dimension is
the number of singular values below 1e-24, and a gap to the remaining values above 1e-8 is
required.
Status of the claims. Everything about C(a, b, c) is a numerical observation. Exact leading
coefficients are necessary conditions, not proofs. Completeness rests on a numerical singular-value
gap, and the claims have scope=punkte. The holomorphic Sturm-bound identities (the only
statements that would count as theorems) are not part of the verified claim set used here, so this
article states no theorems.
A third party re-runs the certificates as described in the Declarations.
The results were produced by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which every statement
was accepted only after code-based verification. Counter-hypotheses were tested adversarially
and the proposing process had no influence on the verdicts.

4

Results

4.1

Relation spaces

The four observations share one design: the C(a, b, c) of weight w plus E(w) and ζ(w).
Numerical observation 1 (Weight 3). Numerically, the rational linear relations among
C(1, 1, 1), E(3), ζ(3) form a space of dimension exactly 1, spanned by C(1, 1, 1) − E(3) − ζ(3) = 0.
2

result may be known.

5

Negative results
• Weight 6. We asked for rational linear relations among C(4, 1, 1), C(3, 2, 1), C(2, 2, 2), E(6),
E(2)E(4), E(3)2 , E(2)3 , ζ(3)E(3), ζ(3)2 , and for the dimension of the relation space (0
would also be a result). No claim passed the verifier. For three attempts the reason is that
no relation was confirmed individually and the 12 × 9 matrix has 0 singular values below
1e-24, 8 above 1e-8, smallest large value 2.44e-8. The fourth attempt returned no verifiable
relation. We therefore state no weight-6 result.
• Eta-quotient identities. No verified claim about eta quotients is available to this article as a
main statement, so no reason for a failure is asserted here. Only adversarial counter-checks
are recorded, in Appendix A.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

All C(a, b, c) statements rest on 32-digit evaluations at 4 verifier points and on singular-value
gaps, which is numerical evidence, not proof. The dimension 1 at each weight is a statement
about the tested function sets. The computation at weight eleven is still running, so no statement
beyond weight 9 is made. The weight-9 relation has inconclusive novelty status.
Open questions:
(i) Is the relation at each weight provable, for example by exact reduction of the lattice sums?
(ii) Does the generating-series counting of arXiv:2004.05156 reproduce the weight-9 relationspace dimension?
(iii) How does the pattern continue at weight eleven?
(iv) Can the weight-6 relation space be determined?

A

Agentic laboratory

The laboratory ran 6 rounds with 21 verified statements and 2 negative results; every round
was preregistered before the experiment (prereg.md). Agents appearing in the weight-6 record

4

 are named sparsam, numeriker, skeptiker and theoretiker. Novelty searches were run per
result, with abstract counts recorded.
Red-team statistics: 25 adversarial counter-checks in total; 2 passed, 22 did not pass, 1 was
not executable. Examples: replacing the ζ(5) source term ζ(5)/10 in the Laplace equation of
C(3, 1, 1) by ζ(5)/5 gives a maximal relative residual 1.04e-01. Changing the coefficient of ζ(9)
to 2 is refuted exactly. The claim that the weight-9 relation space has dimension 0 fails the
singular-value test. A counter-check with an eta quotient whose q 1 coefficient is 9 fails because
the exact coefficient is 8.
